newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW TAB loses A$6.3 million in Hungary betting venture.
newsitem.headline: NSW TAB loses A$6.3 million in Hungary betting venture.

text.p: A state government-owned Australian betting agency has pulled out of a horse racing venture in Hungary with a loss of A$6.3 million, the government said on Tuesday.
New South Wales (NSW) state gaming minister Richard Face said in a statement he had ordered the NSW Totalisator Agency Board (TAB) to end its joint venture with the Hungary Racing Authority.
The TAB had attempted to sell A$1 million of betting equipment it installed in Hungary but the Hungarian authority had been unable to raise the money, Face said.
The NSW TAB signed a 10-year, $A12 million contract in 1991 with the Hungary Racing Authority to install and help operate on-course and off-course totalisator systems for horse racing in Hungary.
The New South Wales government examined the Hungarian venture last year in a review of government spending and concluded it would not return a profit, he said.
